DPOSE combines (1) an ensemble architecture that outputs a collection of target predictions, based on which mean and variance of the ensemble are computed; (2) weight sharing up to the last hidden layer, that reduces the computational overhead and simplifies implementation; (3) training by minimization of the NLL, reducing the need for post-hoc calibration; (4) error estimation on derived quantities through ensemble propagation (see also Figure 3).

results.title: Coupling an agent-based model and an ensemble Kalman filter for real-time crowd modelling | Royal Society Open Science | The Royal Society
results.content: # Coupling an agent-based model and an ensemble Kalman filter for real-time crowd modelling *Open Access*. This paper addresses this challenge by integrating the ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) with an agent-based crowd model to enhance its accuracy in real time. agent-based model, crowd simulation, data assimilation, ensemble Kalman filter, data-driven agent-based modelling. Although other approaches have attempted to leverage data assimilation (DA) techniques for real-time agent-based modelling [13,17–23], and one has even used an EnKF [24], this paper is the first to apply the EnKF to an ABM that contains unique agents and their interactions (both key elements for an ABM [25]) and tests the algorithm using a real-world example of crowd simulation rather than a toy system. In such a situation, we are able to compare the average error per agent in each of the ensemble member models at each assimilation time step. This experiment involves running a collection of EnKFs for the same set of model and filter parameters, and in each case, gathering data regarding the variation in the error in the ensemble mean state over time, comparing this with the variation in the corresponding collection of benchmark errors. Error at the level of the individual agents is quantified by calculating the distance between the position of an agent estimated by the ensemble of models in the EnKF (the ‘ensemble mean state’) and the position of the corresponding agent in the base model, *d**i*:. A vector of average errors per agent for each ensemble member models can then be calculated for each time step. We can now explore how the average error per agent varies across the filter ensemble member models and how this compares to the ensemble mean state. Figure 12 compares the average error per agent in the forecast and analysis states of the filter model ensembles, that is, the error before and after assimilating data at each time step. Finally, figure 13 compares the variation in the average error per agent in the (pseudo-true) observations and the analysis states of the filter model ensembles. Developing methods for real-time pedestrian agent-based modelling: an ensemble Kalman filter approach.

results.content: You are here: Home1 / Blog2 / Publications3 / Uncertainty Propagation on LLM Agent. # Uncertainty Propagation on LLM Agent. /in Publications/by NEC Labs America. **Abstract:** Large language models (LLMs) integrated into multi-step agent systems enable complex decision-making processes across various applications. Existing uncertainty estimation methods primarily focus on final-step outputs, which fail to account for cumulative uncertainty over the multi-step decision-making process and the dynamic interactions between agents and their environments. results.title: Propagation and Amplification of Local Productivity Spillovers | The Econometric Society
results.content: ## Journal Of The Econometric Society. Home> Publications> Econometrica>Propagation and Amplification of Local Productivity Spillovers. # Propagation and Amplification of Local Productivity Spillovers. Using confidential Census plant‐level data, we show that large industrial plant openings raise the productivity not only of local plants but also of distant plants hundreds of miles away, which belong to large multi‐plant, multi‐region firms that are exposed to the local productivity spillover through one of their plants. To quantify the significance of firms' plant‐level networks for the propagation and amplification of local productivity shocks, we estimate a quantitative spatial model in which plants of multi‐region firms are linked through shared knowledge. “Propagation and Amplification of Local Productivity Spillovers.” *Econometrica*, vol.
